title: Pull-transition formula for geometric operation data
statement:
theorem semilinearGeometryTransitionExistence (systems : Data.{c, v, r} J B τ)
    {C' : Type c} [Category.{v} C'] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C']
    (J' : GrothendieckTopology C')
    (uInv : Sheaf J (Type (max c v r)) ⥤ Sheaf J' (Type (max c v r)))
    (uPush : Sheaf J' (Type (max c v r)) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type (max c v r)))
    (adjSet : uInv ⊣ uPush) [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv]
    (G : Geometry.{c, v, r} J B τ systems J' uInv uPush adjSet) :
    G.PullTransitionFormula J B τ systems J' uInv uPush adjSet

proof.text: The derived restriction-form transitions are the localizations of the ordinary horizontal maps. Prove their factorization on Q-images of complexes directly from derivedTransition. For arbitrary exact functor squares, compare the two pasted derived natural transformations by localization extensionality. Postcompose with the invertible exact-functor factorization maps; naturality reduces the equality to the ordinary transition square in each cochain degree. Apply this result to Geometry.ordinaryPullTransition and use Geometry.pullEvaluation_model to obtain the derived restriction-form pull-transition square.

proof.text: Apply the target scalar adjunction homEquiv to the desired extension-form equation. Its left- and right-naturality laws turn the equation into the derived restriction-form square from the first step. Indeed coefficientPullback_transpose identifies the transpose of the inverse coefficient comparison with inverse image of the source scalar unit followed by localized restrictionPullback. Naturality of restrictionPullback moves the source reduction past this comparison. The source adjunction unit formula and homEquiv.apply_symm_apply identify unit followed by restriction of the source reduction with the actual derived source transition. This is a proved abstract categorical helper, specialized to the given Geometry; no new assumed lemma is introduced.
